samples.summary: `failing?.verdict` never exists on a runner observation, so every reported finding's prediction verdict is always "unknown"
samples.evidence: runHunt builds `record.prediction = { ...expect, verdict: failing?.verdict ?? "unknown" }` where `failing = firstObservations?.[cand.failingIndex]` comes from `runUiPlan`. The runner's `observeAction` (packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:373-383) returns `{index, action, ok, error, value, actual, actualError, oracles}` and explicitly does NOT compute a verdict ("The runner does NOT compare … the verdict is hunt-ui-expect.mjs's to render", line 356). So `failing.verdict` is always `undefined` and the report line `renderUiReport` emits at hunt-ui.mjs:593 always ends in `— unknown`. Two consequences: (a) the maintainer-facing report never shows whether the prediction was violated; (b) nothing in the clean-room path re-runs `assessExpectation`, so the pipeline never confirms the prediction still violates on replay — it only checks that four clean-room runs agree with each other. The unit fixture FUNNEL_OBS in hunt-ui.test.mjs invents `verdict: "violated"` on observations, which is exactly the hand-written-fixture-asserting-a-property-the-pipeline-lacks failure the file's own comments warn about, and it is why no test catches this.

samples.summary: `--fault` with no value passes the new kebab-case validation (regex tested against the string "undefined") and silently produces a CLEAN run
samples.evidence: `else if (a === "--fault") out.fault = argv[++i];` sets `out.fault = undefined` when `--fault` is the last argument. The new guard is `if (out.fault !== null && !/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(out.fault))` — `undefined !== null` is true, and `RegExp.test(undefined)` coerces to the string "undefined", which matches the pattern, so no error is thrown. Downstream `const seed = fault ? ... : ""` (line 244) is falsy, so the run proceeds with no fault injected. The operator asked for a seeded positive control and gets an inert one that reports success — precisely the failure mode the control exists to detect. Use `typeof out.fault !== "string"` or check for a missing value at parse time.

samples.summary: `replayUiCandidate` wraps each attempt in a single-element array, defeating `replay()`'s empty-attempt fail-closed guard
samples.evidence: `runAttempt: (_actions, i) => [pre[i]]` always returns a length-1 outer array, so `replay()`'s `const ran = Array.isArray(observations) && observations.length > 0` (hunt-probe.mjs:406) is true even when `pre[i]` is `[]` or `undefined` — the exact 'attempt that never ran anything' case that check was added to fail closed on. The inner emptiness is then keyed by `uiPlanKey([])`/`uiPlanKey(undefined)`, which both yield the same `n:0|…` key. If the claimed `firstObservations` is also empty/undefined (e.g. a stubbed or degraded runner returning `[[]]`), all four keys match and the candidate is marked `reproduced` + `deterministic` without a single action having executed. Production reachability is low (assertSafeActionPlan forbids an empty action list), but the guard the code relies on is not actually in force here; the `runAttempt` wrapper should return `[]` when `pre[i]` is missing or empty.

samples.summary: `--fault` is shape-validated everywhere but never checked against the closed fault registry, so an unknown-but-well-formed id yields a run labelled SEEDED that is not seeded
samples.evidence: `cmdRun` takes `--fault` as an arbitrary string; hunt-ui-probe.mjs:286, hunt-ui-session.mjs:107 and the runner only check kebab-case shape. The page's registry is `KNOWN_FAULTS = ["drop-second-char"]` (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:83) and an unknown id degrades to `data-hunt-harness-fault="none"` — deliberately. Combined, `--fault drop-secnd-char` runs an ordinary hunt while `renderUiReport` stamps the report 'SEEDED RUN — NOT A HUNT … MANUFACTURED and must not be filed' and `cmdRun` skips the ledger write. Real findings from that run are labelled fabricated and lose their ledger record, and a developer expecting the positive control gets a clean run. Nothing shares the known-fault id list between the page and the orchestrator.

samples.summary: An invalid `--surface` value fails with the misleading 'no personas selected' before the specific surface check runs
samples.evidence: `selectPersonas` runs first, excluding every persona for an unrecognised surface; `if (personas.length === 0) fail("no personas selected")` on line 839 then exits before the loop on lines 840-842 that would have said `--surface "docs" is not one of: doc, sheet`. `parseArgs` also pushes the boolean `true` into `args.surface` when `--surface` is given without a value, which hits the same misleading path. Swap the two blocks.

samples.summary: The file header still asserts an invariant this change deletes — 'There is no `?fault=` query parameter and no test-only branch in the harness route'
samples.evidence: Lines 14-16 state: 'Faults are injected from the DRIVER, never from application code. There is no `?fault=` query parameter and no test-only branch in the harness route — the page under test is the page that ships, and Playwright supplies the damage.' The same file now contains `checkSeededFault`, which navigates to `?fault=drop-second-char`, and page.tsx now carries `installFault`. A reader (or a future reviewer) taking this comment as the contract will conclude the fault route is illegitimate or that the seeded control is a leftover.

samples.summary: `checkSeededFaultInServeMode` reads `doc.text` with an unsettled `read` action immediately after typing, so this CI-gating lane can flake
samples.evidence: `await session.act({type:"type", text: FAULT_TYPED}); const read = await session.act({type:"read", reader:"doc.text"})`. A plain `read` goes through `readValue` in the runner (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:277) with no settling loop — only `observeAction`'s fixed 30 ms wait — whereas the prediction path deliberately uses `readSettled` because 'the text lands asynchronously relative to the keystrokes'. The sibling checks in this same file (checkUndoCapability, typeIntoDoc) poll for settlement for exactly this reason; this new one does not, so a slow machine can read stale text and fail the lane.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository exactly as described. The runner's observeAction (packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:372-383) returns {index, action, ok, error, value, actual?, actualError?, oracles} with no `verdict`, and its own comment (lines 356-358) says the runner does not compare. runUiPlan (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:328) returns those observations unmodified. runHunt therefore reads a field that never exists: scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:1078 takes `failing = firstObservations?.[cand.failingIndex]` from runPlanImpl (line 1071), and line 1096 sets `verdict: failing?.verdict ?? "unknown"`, so the value is unconditionally "unknown". The renderer at hunt-ui.mjs:593 prints that value, so every reported prediction line ends in "— unknown". Grep across **/*.mjs confirms assessExpectation is used only in the live-session tool path (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.mjs:44,366), never in hunt-ui.mjs or hunt-ui-probe.mjs, so the clean-room/replay path never re-evaluates the prediction — replayUiCandidate (hunt-ui.mjs:478-486) only compares uiPlanKey across attempts. The unit fixture that would have caught this invents the field: hunt-ui.test.mjs:636-643 and :758 add `verdict: "violated"` to observations the runner never produces, injected via runPlanImpl at :665. No guard, caller, or alternate code path makes this unreachable, and it is a genuine logic/correctness defect (dead field feeding maintainer-facing output plus an unperformed re-check), so it is in this lens's lane.

verdict.reason: Verified directly in the repository. hunt-ui-runner.mjs:72 assigns `out.fault = argv[++i]`, which is `undefined` when `--fault` is the last argument (and the loop then exits without hitting the unknown-argument throw at :73). The new guard at :79 is `out.fault !== null && !/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(out.fault)`: `undefined !== null` is true, and `RegExp.test` coerces `undefined` to the string "undefined", which matches the kebab-case pattern, so the negation is false and no error is thrown. `args.fault` then flows to :528/:533 and reaches runAction, where :244 `const seed = fault ? ... : ""` is falsy, so :245 navigates without a `&fault=` query param and the run proceeds with no defect injected, reporting a normal result. The wrapper call sites (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:309 and scripts/agent/hunt-ui-session.mjs:118) always spread `["--fault", String(fault)]` only when fault is truthy, so they do not exercise this path — but they are not a guard: the file's own comment at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:131-134 states the driver is invocable directly, and direct CLI usage with `--fault <id>` is documented at scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:35. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. This is a missing/incorrect validation condition causing a silent failure of a positive control — in the Correctness lane, and major impact since the operator gets a CLEAN report from an inert control.
